translations.idiomatic: Xi's brother Daocun was Yellow Gate personnel officer and Nan Commandery Grand Administrator.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勳建偽號，以為侍中，行雍州事，事敗見殺。

translations.literal: When Prince Xun of Jin'an established a false reign, Daocun was made Palace Attendant acting in Yong Province affairs; when the affair failed he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xun of Jin'an declared a rival throne, Daocun became acting Yongzhou governor as Palace Attendant; the revolt failed and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 殷景仁，陳郡長平人也。

translations.literal: Yin Jingren was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren came from Changping in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖融，晉太常。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong was Grand Minister of Ceremonies of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong had been Jin Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 祖茂之，特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Maozhi was Special Grand Master and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Maozhi was Special Grand Master and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 父道裕，早亡。

translations.literal: His father Daoyu died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoyu died young.

sentences.zh: 景仁少有大成之量，司徒王謐見而以女妻之。

translations.literal: Jingren from youth had the measure of great accomplishment; Minister of Education Wang Mi saw him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren showed early promise of greatness; Minister of Education Wang Mi married him to his daughter.

sentences.zh: 為宋武帝太尉行參軍，歷位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Staff Officer to Emperor Wu of Song's Grand Commandant and held successive posts to Gentleman in the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liu Yu's Grand Commandant as acting staff officer and rose to Central Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 景仁不為文而敏有思致，不談義而深達理，至於國典朝儀，舊章記注，莫不撰錄，識者知其有當世之志也。

translations.literal: Jingren did not compose literature yet was quick with thoughtful insight; he did not discuss principle yet deeply grasped reason; as for state canon and court ritual, old regulations and annotations, he compiled none that he did not record—those who knew saw he had ambition for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren wrote no essays yet thought with precision; he debated no abstractions yet understood principle deeply; state law, court ritual, old statutes—he recorded them all, and observers knew he meant to shape his age.

sentences.zh: 文帝所生章太后早亡，上奉太后所生蘇氏甚謹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's biological mother Empress Dowager Zhang died early; the emperor served the Empress Dowager's mother Lady Su with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's birth mother Empress Dowager Zhang had died young; the emperor cared meticulously for her mother Lady Su.

sentences.zh: 六年，蘇氏卒，車駕親往臨哭，詔欲遵二漢推恩之典。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Lady Su died; the imperial carriage went in person to mourn, and an edict wished to follow the Han precedent of extending favor.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Lady Su died; the emperor mourned in person and proposed extending favor as the Han had done.

sentences.zh: 景仁議以為「漢氏推恩加爵，于時承秦之弊，儒術蔑如，懼非盛明所宜軌蹈。

translations.literal: Jingren argued that 'Han extension of favor and addition of nobility came when inheriting Qin's decay and Confucian learning was scorned—I fear this is not what a flourishing sage should follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren argued that Han ennoblement of kin arose from Qin's ruin when learning was despised—not a model for a flourishing sage reign.

sentences.zh: 晉監二代，朝政之所因，君舉必書，哲王之所慎。

translations.literal: Jin watched two dynasties and was what court governance followed; the ruler's every act was recorded—what wise kings guarded carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Jin watched Han and Wei and shaped court practice; a wise king's every act is written—this is what sage rulers guard.

sentences.zh: 體至公者懸爵賞於無私，奉天統者每屈情以申制，所以作孚萬國，貽則後昆」。

translations.literal: Embodying utmost publicness hangs rewards on selflessness; holding heaven's mandate often bends feeling to uphold regulation—thus trust is made among the myriad states and example left to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Utmost fairness hangs rewards on merit alone; heaven's mandate often bends private feeling to law—thus the realm trusts the throne and posterity inherits the rule.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，葬竟，起為領軍將軍，固辭。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when burial was complete he was recalled as Director of the Guard and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's burial he was recalled as Director of the Guard and refused.

sentences.zh: 上使綱紀代拜，遣中書舍人周赳輿載詣府。

translations.literal: The emperor had the household steward perform the bow in his stead and sent Palace Attendant Zhou Jiu in a carriage to convey him to the office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a proxy perform the acceptance rite and sent Secretary Zhou Jiu in a carriage to haul him to office.

sentences.zh: 服闋，遷尚書僕射。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事劉湛代為領軍，湛與景仁素善，皆被遇于武帝，俱以宰相許之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent Liu Zhan replaced him as Director of the Guard; Zhan and Jingren had long been on good terms, both favored by Emperor Wu, and both were promised the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince tutor Liu Zhan replaced him as Guard Director; Zhan and Jingren were old allies, both favored by Liu Yu, both marked for chancellor.

sentences.zh: 湛常居外任。

translations.literal: Zhan often held outer appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan usually served in provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 會王弘、王華、王曇首相系亡，景仁引湛還朝，共參朝政。

translations.literal: When Wang Hong, Wang Hua, and Wang Tanshou died in succession, Jingren brought Zhan back to court to join in governing.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Hong, Wang Hua, and Wang Tanshou died in turn, Jingren recalled Zhan to share governance.

sentences.zh: 湛既入，以景仁位遇本不踰己，一旦居前，意甚憤憤。

translations.literal: Once Zhan entered, because Jingren's rank and favor had originally not exceeded his own yet suddenly stood before him, his resentment was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Once back at court Zhan saw Jingren—once his equal—suddenly above him, and rage consumed him.

sentences.zh: 知文帝信仗景仁，不可移奪，乃深結司徒彭城王義康，欲倚宰相之重以傾之。

translations.literal: Knowing Emperor Wen trusted and relied on Jingren and he could not be moved aside, he deeply allied with Minister of Education Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, wishing to lean on the chancellor's weight to overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor would not abandon Jingren, Zhan bonded with Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, hoping the prince's weight would topple his rival.

sentences.zh: 十二年，景仁遷中書令、護軍將軍，僕射如故，尋復加領吏部。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Jingren was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and General Who Protects the Army, Vice Director unchanged, and soon additionally given charge of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve Jingren became Secretariat Director and Protecting Army General, kept the vice directorship, and soon took Personnel as well.

sentences.zh: 湛愈怒，義康納湛言，毀景仁于文帝，帝遇之益隆。

translations.literal: Zhan grew angrier; Prince Yikang took Zhan's words and slandered Jingren to Emperor Wen, yet the emperor treated Jingren with ever greater honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan fumed; Prince Yikang whispered against Jingren to the emperor—and the emperor honored Jingren all the more.

sentences.zh: 景仁密陳相王權重，非社稷計，上以為然。

translations.literal: Jingren secretly reported that the prince's power was too heavy for the state's good; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren secretly warned that the prince's power threatened the realm; the emperor concurred.

sentences.zh: 景仁對親舊歎曰：「引之令入，便噬人。

translations.literal: Jingren sighed to kin and friends, 'I brought him in and he bites.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren told friends, 'I invited him in—and he bites the hand.

sentences.zh: 」乃稱疾請解，不見許，使停家養病。

translations.literal: He then pleaded illness to resign but was not permitted; he was ordered to stop at home and nurse his illness.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned illness to resign; the emperor refused and ordered him to convalesce at home.

sentences.zh: 湛議欲遣人若劫盜者於外殺之，以為文帝雖知，當不能傷至親之愛。

translations.literal: Zhan debated sending men like bandits to kill him outside; he thought Emperor Wen though knowing would not harm the love of close kin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan plotted hired killers outside the walls, betting the emperor would not punish close kin even if he learned of it.

sentences.zh: 上微聞之，徙景仁於西掖門外晉鄱陽主第，以為護軍府。

translations.literal: The emperor faintly heard of this and moved Jingren to the Jin Princess of Poyang's residence outside the Western Side Gate, making it the Protecting Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor caught wind and moved Jingren to Princess Poyang's mansion outside the Western Side Gate as Protecting Army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 密邇宮禁，故其計不行。

translations.literal: Close to the palace precinct, therefore the plot could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The palace walls were too close—Zhan's plot failed.

sentences.zh: 景仁臥疾者五年，雖不見上，而密函去來，日中以十數，朝政大小必以問焉。

translations.literal: Jingren lay ill five years; though he did not see the emperor, secret letters came and went—ten or more by midday—and great and small court affairs were always referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren 'sick' for five years never saw the emperor yet exchanged a dozen secret letters by noon daily—every major decision ran through him.

sentences.zh: 影跡周密，莫有窺其際者。

translations.literal: His traces were tightly guarded; none could glimpse his edge.
translations.idiomatic: His network was sealed tight; no spy pierced it.

sentences.zh: 及將收湛之日，景仁便拂拭衣冠。

translations.literal: On the day Prince Yikang and Zhan were to be arrested, Jingren at once brushed robes and cap.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Liu Zhan and Prince Yikang were seized, Jingren dressed at once.

sentences.zh: 寢疾既久，左右皆不悟其意。

translations.literal: Bedridden so long, those around him did not grasp his intent.
translations.idiomatic: After years abed his attendants did not understand.

sentences.zh: 其夜，上出華林園延賢堂召之，景仁猶稱腳疾，小床輿以就坐，誅討處分，一皆委之。

translations.literal: That night the emperor came out to the Hall of Worthies in Huaglin Garden and summoned him; Jingren still claimed foot ailment and came seated on a small couch; execution and disposition were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor summoned him to the Hall of Worthies; Jingren came on a litter claiming gout—and received full authority over the purge.

sentences.zh: 代義康為揚州刺史，僕射、吏部如故。

translations.literal: Replacing Prince Yikang as Governor of Yang Province, Vice Director and Personnel unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Prince Yikang as Yangzhou governor while keeping Vice Director and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 遣使者授印綬，主簿代拜畢，便覺疾甚，情理乖錯。

translations.literal: An envoy delivered seal and cord; the chief clerk performed the bow in his stead; when that was done he suddenly felt very ill and his mind went awry.
translations.idiomatic: After the proxy acceptance of Yangzhou seals his mind broke.

sentences.zh: 性本寬厚，而忽更苛暴，問左右曰：「今年男婚多，女嫁多？

translations.literal: His nature was originally generous, yet suddenly he turned harsh and violent, asking those around, 'This year are more sons marrying or more daughters marrying?
translations.idiomatic: Naturally mild, he turned savage and asked servants, 'Are more sons marrying this year or more daughters?

sentences.zh: 」是冬大雪，景仁乘輿出廳事觀望，忽驚曰：「當閣何得有大樹？

translations.literal: That winter snow fell heavily; Jingren rode out to the hall to look and suddenly cried in alarm, 'How can there be a great tree in the gate pavilion?
translations.idiomatic: Heavy winter snow fell; Jingren rode to the hall, stared, and cried, 'Why is there a great tree in the gate?

sentences.zh: 」既而曰：「我誤耳。

translations.literal: Then he said, 'I am mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Then he muttered, 'My mistake.

sentences.zh: 」疾篤，文帝謂不利在州，使還住僕射下省。

translations.literal: His illness grew grave; Emperor Wen said the ill omen lay in the province and had him return to lodge at the Vice Director's lower office.
translations.idiomatic: As he worsened the emperor blamed Yangzhou and moved him back to the Vice Director's quarters.

sentences.zh: 為州凡月餘日卒，或云見劉湛為祟。

translations.literal: As governor barely a month more he died; some said he was haunted by Liu Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: He died barely a month after taking the province; some said Liu Zhan's ghost hounded him.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、司空，諡曰文成公。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, with posthumous title Duke Wen of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, titled Duke Wen of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 大明五年，孝武行經景仁墓，詔遣致祭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu passed Jingren's tomb and ordered offerings sent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 5 Emperor Xiaowu passed Jingren's tomb and ordered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子道矜，幼而不慧，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: His son Daojin was dull from youth and held the post of Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daojin was slow-witted from childhood and became Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 道矜子恒，明帝時，位侍中、度支尚書。

translations.literal: Daojin's son Heng, in Emperor Ming's time, held the posts of Palace Attendant and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Daojin's son Heng served Emperor Ming as Palace Attendant and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 屬父疾積久，為有司所奏。

translations.literal: Because his father's illness had long accumulated, he was impeached by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had long nursed his ailing father, officials impeached him for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「道矜生便有病，更無橫疾；

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Daojin was sick from birth and had no sudden illness;
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: 'Daojin has been ill since birth—no sudden affliction;

sentences.zh: 恒因愚習惰，久妨清序，可除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Heng through foolish habit and sloth long obstructed clear order—he may be removed from Regular Attendant of the Privy.
translations.idiomatic: Heng through sloth and stupidity long blocked proper service—strip him of Privy Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 」淳字粹遠，景仁從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Chun, courtesy name Cuiyuan, was Jingren's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Chun styled Cuiyuan was Jingren's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖允，晉太常。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun was Grand Minister of Ceremonies of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun had been Jin Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 父穆，以和謹致稱，自五兵尚書為宋武帝相國左長史。

translations.literal: His father Mu was famed for harmony and prudence and rose from Minister of the Five Armies to Left Chief of Staff to Emperor Wu of Song's Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mu, famed for gentle prudence, rose from Minister of War to chief secretary under Liu Yu's chancellery.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，位特進、右光祿大夫，領始興王師。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he held Special Grand Master and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanjia he was Special Grand Master and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, tutoring the Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰元子。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous title was Master Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office with posthumous title Master Yuan.

sentences.zh: 淳少好學，有美名，曆中書黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Chun from youth loved learning and had a fine reputation; he held successive posts to Gentleman in the Yellow Gate of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Chun loved learning from youth and won a fine name, rising to Secretariat Gentleman in the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 黃門清切，直下應留下省，以父老特聽還家。

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate was pure and urgent and normally required staying overnight in the lower office; because his father was old he was specially permitted to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate duty normally required overnight stays at the lower office; because his father was aged he was allowed home.

sentences.zh: 高簡寡言，早有清尚，愛好文義，未嘗違舍。

translations.literal: Lofty and sparing of words, early he had pure aspiration, loved literary principle, and never strayed from his lodgings.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved and terse, he cherished pure ambition and letters and rarely left his study.

sentences.zh: 在秘書閣撰四部書大目，凡四十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat he compiled the great catalogue of the Four Libraries, forty volumes in all, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat he compiled the forty-volume catalogue of the Four Libraries, published to the world.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十一年卒，朝廷痛惜之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia he died; the court grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanjia 11; the court mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 子孚有父風。

translations.literal: His son Fu had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu inherited his father's character.

sentences.zh: 嘗與侍中何勖共食，孚羹盡，勖云：「益殷蓴羹。

translations.literal: Once he dined with Palace Attendant He Xu; Fu's soup was finished and Xu said, 'More Yin lotus soup.
translations.idiomatic: Dining with Palace Attendant He Xu, Fu finished his soup; Xu called, 'More Yin-lotus soup.

sentences.zh: 」勖司空無忌子也，孚徐輟箸曰：「何無忌諱。

translations.literal: Xu was Minister of Works Wuji's son; Fu slowly set down his chopsticks and said, 'He Wuji is taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was son of Minister He Wuji; Fu set down his chopsticks: 'The name Wuji is taboo.

sentences.zh: 」孚位吏部郎，為順帝撫軍長史。

translations.literal: Fu held the post of Gentleman in the Personnel section and was Chief Administrator to the Pacification Army of Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was a personnel officer and chief secretary to Emperor Shun's pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 子臻字後同，幼有名行，袁粲、褚彥回並賞異之。

translations.literal: His son Zhen, courtesy name Houtong, from youth had fame for conduct; Yuan Can and Chu Yuan both admired and distinguished him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's son Zhen styled Houtong was famed for conduct from youth; Yuan Can and Chu Yuan both marked him out.

sentences.zh: 每造二公之席，輒清言畢景。

translations.literal: Whenever he visited the two lords' seats, pure talk ran to the end of the scene.
translations.idiomatic: At their tables his conversation ran clear to the day's end.

sentences.zh: 王儉為丹陽尹，引為郡丞。

translations.literal: Wang Jian as Intendant of Danyang recruited him as commandery aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian was Danyang Intendant he recruited Zhen as commandery aide.

sentences.zh: 袁昂先拜秘書丞，求臻為到省表。

translations.literal: Yuan Ang had first been appointed Secretariat Assistant and asked Zhen to draft the arrival memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang, newly made Secretariat Assistant, asked Zhen to draft his arrival memorial.

sentences.zh: 臻答曰：「何不見倩拜，而見倩作表。

translations.literal: Zhen answered, 'Why not ask me to perform the bow and yet ask me to compose the memorial?
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, 'You ask me to bow for you but not to write your memorial?

sentences.zh: 」遂不為作。

translations.literal: He therefore did not compose it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 歷位太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He held successive posts to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 淳弟沖字希遠，位御史中丞，有司直之稱。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Chong, courtesy name Xiyuan, held the post of Censor-in-Chief and was called straight by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's brother Chong styled Xiyuan became Censor-in-Chief and was called the court's straight edge.

sentences.zh: 再遷度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元凶妃即淳女，而沖在東宮為劭所知遇。

translations.literal: The Deposed Heir's consort was Chun's daughter, yet Chong in the Eastern Palace was known and favored by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Heir Liu Shao's consort was Chun's daughter, yet Chong served Shao in the Eastern Palace and won his favor.

sentences.zh: 劭弑立，以為司隸校尉。

translations.literal: When Shao usurped and established himself he made Chong Director of the Masters of Correctness.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao seized the throne he made Chong Director of the Masters of Correctness.

sentences.zh: 沖有學義文辭，劭使為尚書符，罪狀孝武，亦為劭盡力。

translations.literal: Chong had learning, righteousness, and literary skill; Shao had him compose the Masters of Writing proclamation condemning Emperor Xiaowu, and Chong also exerted himself fully for Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and eloquent, Chong drafted Shao's indictment of Emperor Xiaowu and served the usurper with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 建鄴平，賜死。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell he was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 沖弟淡字夷遠，亦曆黃門吏部郎，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Dan, courtesy name Yiyuan, also held successive posts as Gentleman in the Yellow Gate Personnel section and Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's brother Dan styled Yiyuan served as Yellow Gate personnel officer and crown prince companion.

sentences.zh: 大明中，又以文章見知。

translations.literal: In the Daming era he was again known for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daming he won notice again for his writing.

sentences.zh: 論曰：季恭命偶興王，恩深惟舊，及位致崇寵，而每存謙挹。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Ji Gong's fate paired him with a rising king; his favor ran deep as an old companion, and when he reached lofty honor he still kept humility.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Ji Gong's lot paired him with a rising sovereign; though deeply favored he stayed humble at the height of honor.

sentences.zh: 觀夫持滿之戒，足以追蹤古人。

translations.literal: Consider his warning against holding the cup full—enough to follow the ancients' track.
translations.idiomatic: His heed of the full-cup warning lets him stand with the ancients.

sentences.zh: 琇之貞素之風，不踐無義之地。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's integrity and plainness—he would not tread ground without righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's austere integrity kept him off unrighteous ground.

sentences.zh: 易曰：「王臣蹇蹇，其動也直。

translations.literal: The Changes say: 'The king's minister, arduous and arduous—his movement is straight.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: 'The king's minister, steadfast and straight in action.

sentences.zh: 」休文行己之度，可謂近之。

translations.literal: Xiuwen's measure in conducting himself can be called near to this.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiuwen's conduct approached that standard.

sentences.zh: 琳之二議，深達變通之道。

translations.literal: Linzhi's two memorials deeply grasped the way of flexible change.
translations.idiomatic: Linzhi's twin memorials mastered the art of adaptive governance.

sentences.zh: 覬持身之節，亦曰一時之良，而聽言則悖，晚致覆沒，痛矣哉！

translations.literal: Xi's integrity in self-conduct was also called a worthy of the age, yet in hearing counsel he was perverse and in late years met ruin—painful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Xi held his body with integrity and was called a man of the age—yet he deafened himself to counsel and ended in ruin. A bitter end.

sentences.zh: 景仁遠大之情，著于初筮，元嘉之盛，卒致宗臣，言聽計從，於斯為重，美矣乎。

translations.literal: Jingren's far-reaching intent was evident from the first divination; in Yuanjia's flourishing he finally became a pillar of the state, his words heard and plans followed—here lay the weight, and how fine!
translations.idiomatic: Jingren's breadth showed from the first oracle; in Yuanjia's glory he became the state's pillar, every word heeded—there lay true weight, and how fine a life.
